toolmode-targeted-search: Targeted Search Mode (Long range, sample-guided search)
mod-description: Adds a sample-guided search mode to the prospecting pick for locating matching ore and mineral deposits in the surrounding area.
require-prospecting-pick: Hold a prospecting pick in your main hand.
require-durability: The prospecting pick has only {0}% durability remaining. At least 80% durability is required to begin targeted prospecting.
require-reference-sample: Hold an ore nugget, ore chunk, crystallized ore chunk, or supported mineral sample in your off hand.
requirements-ready: Ready to begin targeted prospecting. Sample: {0}. Prospecting pick durability: {1}%.
command-check-description: Checks and tells the player whether they are ready to begin Targeted Prospecting.
command-logger-description: Controls the Targeted Prospecting test logger.
command-logger-start-description: Starts the mod test logger and creates a new log file for mod diagnostics.
command-logger-stop-description: Stops the active mod test logger.
logger-already-active: Targeted Prospecting test logger is already active.
logger-start-failed: Targeted Prospecting test logger could not be started. See the server log for details.
logger-not-active: Targeted Prospecting test logger is not active.
command-cooldown-description: Commands for managing the targeted prospecting cooldown.
command-cooldown-reset-description: Resets the current cooldown for the next Targeted Prospecting survey. Available only in Creative mode.
cooldown-reset-creative-only: The targeted prospecting cooldown can only be reset in Creative mode.
survey-interrupted: Moving the prospecting pick interrupted targeted prospecting.
survey-cooldown: Targeted prospecting will be available again in {0} game hours.
unknown-mineral: The mineral in the reference sample could not be identified.
satiety-drained: Targeted prospecting drained up to 50% of your maximum satiety.
unsupported-pick-material: A prospecting pick made from this material cannot be used for targeted prospecting.

result-multiple-deposits: Matching deposit {0} of {1} was found at X {2}, Z {3}. Mineral: {4}. Depth unknown.
handbook-targeted-prospecting-text:
Found signs of a particular ore, but still cannot locate the actual deposit?

Targeted Prospecting lets you use a sample of the material you are looking for and a prospecting pick to search for an actual deposit in the wider surrounding area. It does not replace ordinary geological prospecting – it follows on from it once you already know what you want to find.

What you need

To prospect, you need:
• a prospecting pick with at least 80% durability,
• a sample of the material you are looking for in your off hand.

A supported nugget, ore chunk, or crystallized chunk of the material can be used as the sample.

How to prospect

Hold the prospecting pick in your main hand and the desired sample in your off hand.

Press F and select Targeted Search Mode (Long range, sample-guided search).

You can begin prospecting anywhere as long as you break rock with the prospecting pick.

The search progresses while the rock is being broken. Breaking must not be interrupted and takes longer than ordinary mining.

When a deposit is found

If a suitable deposit is found, its location is marked with a waypoint on the map.

Targeted Prospecting shows you a place to travel to. You still have to locate and mine the ore itself in the normal way.

The exact depth / elevation of the deposit is not known from the survey.

When nothing is found

Not every survey has to end with a find if the ore you are looking for is not present nearby.

An unsuccessful survey is not entirely free either. The tool takes standard wear and the character consumes the same satiety as during a successful survey.

Survey cost

A successful targeted survey consumes a larger portion of the prospecting pick durability and a significant portion of the character's satiety.

After the survey is completed, a 24 in-game hour cooldown begins, representing fatigue after the demanding search. Until the cooldown ends, another targeted survey cannot be started.

The cooldown and satiety cost also apply if no suitable deposit is found.

On an unsuccessful survey, the prospecting pick takes only standard wear.

It is therefore worth choosing carefully which material you want to search for before beginning a survey.

Prospecting pick material

A better prospecting pick material allows you to obtain more results from one survey.

• Copper – up to 1 result
• All bronze variants – up to 2 results
• Iron and meteoric iron – up to 3 results
• Steel – up to 4 results

A steel prospecting pick also has a special advantage.

Steel prospecting pick bonus

When using a steel prospecting pick, the survey may also reveal certain rare gemstones in addition to the deposit being searched for.

The bonus applies to diamond, emerald, and peridot.

If suitable gemstones are found during the survey, one of them may be selected as a bonus find and its position marked on the map.

Recycling a worn prospecting pick

You do not have to simply throw away an old prospecting pick. You can continue using it for geological prospecting.

Alternatively, these prospecting picks can be dismantled using a saw, hammer, and chisel to recover some of the metal as metal bits of the same material.

The recipe in the handbook shows the maximum yield of 20 metal bits.

The actual number of bits recovered depends on the remaining durability of the prospecting pick. For example, a pick with approximately 50% durability returns 10 metal bits.

The minimum recycling yield is 1 metal bit.

The better preserved the prospecting pick, the more metal can be recovered.
